_comment: Source of truth for main branch protection. Apply with: gh api repos/Smith-Horn/skillsmith/branches/main/protection -X PUT --input .github/branch-protection.json UPDATED 2026-10-03: this file had drifted TWO contexts behind live protection, and the drift direction matters -- `--fix` applies THIS FILE to GitHub, so running it would have REMOVED a required check rather than added one. `pointer-check` (the docs/internal gitlink ancestry gate, ADR-143) was added to live protection and never recorded here; `Edge Functions Typecheck` (SMI-6897) is added by the same commit that recorded it live. Both are now listed. The validator is not wired into CI, so nothing was failing -- which is exactly why the drift survived. SECOND FINDING, same review: a PUT replaces the WHOLE protection object, so any live setting absent from this file is reset to its API default -- and `validate-branch-protection.sh --dry-run` compares only five things (contexts, strict, enforce_admins, allow_force_pushes, allow_deletions), so it would never report drift in the rest. That asymmetry is destructive: enable `required_conversation_resolution` or `required_linear_history` in the GitHub UI and the validator reports clean while the next `--fix` silently switches it back off. The five keys below `allow_deletions` were therefore added to close it -- each written at its CURRENT live value (all false, measured 2026-10-04), so adding them changes nothing today and makes a future `--fix` idempotent instead of normalising. Do not 'tidy' them away as redundant defaults; being written down IS the point. `required_signatures` is live-but-absent here too and was deliberately NOT added: it is believed to be managed by its own `/protection/required_signatures` endpoint rather than this PUT body, which is UNVERIFIED -- there is no way to test it without mutating live protection, so it is recorded as an open gap rather than guessed at. Widening the validator's comparison set is tracked separately and is ADR-109-gated (`scripts/`).
